reasons: AC1 and AC2 bind to ac1-*/ac2-* nodes; trace shows 28/28 nodes ok on the recorded run.
AC2 stages the real race (order cancelled out of band while the dialog is open), so HyperLiquid returns the ticket's rejection rather than a mock.
The baseline recipe run on unmodified sources asserts the opposite outcome and passes, so reverting the change flips AC2 to FAIL.
AC3-AC5 are proven by unit tests with a concrete reason why no manifest action can stage them.

graph_integrity.reason: Single entry, every node reachable, terminal end node, no switch/default routing around an assertion.

action_contract.reason: Only manifest-declared actions; high-level metamask.perps.* actions build and tear down state instead of raw UI setup steps.

ac_coverage.reason: Both recipe-bound claims map to ac<N>-* nodes with provider-side assertions; the three remaining claims are unit-tested with rationale.

evidence_contract_basics.reason: The visual claim is captured after a ui.wait_for on the claimed toast; the screenshot shows the dismissed dialog and the neutral notice, paired with a matching baseline capture. Provider is capture-helper.

perps_state_setup.reason: start_state / ensure_orders / close_orders build the required testnet order state; nothing is declared untestable for missing perps state.

contextual_findings.message: metamask.wallet.select_account fails its own read-back on the first attempt after a fresh launch (reads the pre-selection id). The recipe needs the account selected once beforehand; reported as harness feedback, not a product defect.

suggested_recipe_delta: Graduate the stale-cancel scenario to the perps recipe library once the ticket lands — it is a reusable regression guard for any provider that rejects cancels for closed orders.

good_patterns: baseline run on stashed sources proves the recipe fails without the change
race staged with a real out-of-band provider mutation instead of a mock
